title: On-foot character movement: walk, run, jump, terrain
description: Server-authoritative character movement in surface regime: walk and run speeds, jump with gravity, terrain following (no tunneling), and client-side smoothing for remote characters.
acceptanceCriteria: src/shared/physics/character.ts: integrateCharacter(state, input, dt, heightAt): walk 3 u/s, run 6 u/s (shift), jump impulse 5 u/s (1.2 s airtime), gravity 12 u/s², friction on ground (decel 8 u/s²), no air control (input ignored horizontally while airborne)

Terrain: character y = heightAt(x,z) when on ground (slopes followed smoothly — y is lerped toward terrain at 20 u/s to avoid stair-stepping on steep slopes); substep integration when horizontal speed * dt > 1 m (no tunneling through cliffs in the seeded terrain, which has max slope 45° by TASK-5 constraints)
Jump: only from ground state; can jump off slopes; no double jump; landing is silent (no landing animation in v1)
Server: character inputs arrive as the same 'input' message type (regime-aware: the sim routes to integrateCharacter vs integrateShip); position authoritative in snapshots

Client: local character uses the same integrateCharacter for prediction (TASK-14 pattern reused — a CharacterPredictor mirroring the ship predictor); remote characters use the 200 ms interpolation buffer (already built for ships, TASK-14)

Unit tests: speeds, jump arc (apex height ~1.04 m at these numbers — assert), air control ignored, slope following (analytic 30° slope: y tracks within 0.1 m), substep no-tunnel (cliff edge case), determinism (same input sequence → same path, fixture)
Integration test: scripted 30 s of movement (walk/run/jump over seeded terrain) through the sim — path matches the fixture; npm run test green

steps.details: integrateCharacter as specified; state = {pos, vel, onGround, quat (facing only — yaw from input, no pitch/roll)}; heightAt injected (same contract as ship physics).

SimLoop: per entity, integrate by kind (ship → integrateShip, character → integrateCharacter); input message carries the player's activeEntity kind implicitly (the server knows from state — no protocol change).

CharacterPredictor (local) mirroring ShipPredictor structure (TASK-14); remote characters into the existing RemoteEntityBuffer. Character mesh: a simple capsule + head (placeholder) with a facing rotation; livery colors applied (character uses the player's ship livery accent — cosmetic tie-in, cheap).
All listed unit tests + the 30 s scripted path fixture. Run full suite + typecheck.

technicalNotes: Keep character physics dead simple — v1 is walk/run/jump/interact only (PRD scope). No crouching, no swimming (v1 terrain has no water), no climbing.
The 20 u/s terrain-lerp makes slopes look smooth at 10 Hz snapshots; the prediction hides the rest.
